- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to account for potential rebound.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), leading to overshoot; apply dampening factor (e.g., 0.85–0.90 multiplier) to peak forecasts.
- Forecast mean reversion is weak in early horizon (1–3 days), but stronger after 7–10 days; apply smoothing or lagged average correction for longer-term forecasts.
- If sentiment shifts sharply from positive to negative (e.g., 0.67 → -0.33 within 3 days), model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 2–5% immediately after sentiment reversal.
- For 30-day forecasts, model frequently overestimates early in the horizon (first 5–7 days) — apply downward bias of 1–2% for first 5 days, then revert to normal if sentiment remains stable.
